A **prioritization matrix** is a visual or scoring tool that helps you rank tasks, features, or projects based on clear criteria like urgency, importance, effort, or impact.[[1]](https://www.smartsheet.com/priority-matrix-templates)[[2]](https://miro.com/templates/priority-matrix/)

### Common Types of Prioritization Matrices

- **Eisenhower Matrix (Urgency vs. Importance):** Splits work into four quadrants—*Do First* (urgent/important), *Schedule* (important/not urgent), *Delegate* (urgent/not important), and *Eliminate* (neither).[[1]](https://www.projectmanager.com/blog/prioritization-templates)[[2]](https://www.smartsheet.com/priority-matrix-templates)
- **Impact-Effort Matrix (Value vs. Difficulty):** Plots items to find *Quick Wins* (high impact, low effort), *Major Projects* (high impact, high effort), *Fill-Ins* (low impact, low effort), and *Thankless Tasks* (low impact, high effort).[[1]](https://miro.com/templates/priority-matrix/)[[2]](https://asana.com/templates/prioritization-matrix)
- **Weighted Scoring Matrix:** Multiplies multiple factors (such as business value, cost, and risk) by assigned percentage weights to calculate a total score for each project.[[1]](https://www.smartsheet.com/priority-matrix-templates)


---

### Simple 2x2 Impact-Effort Template Layout
| | **Low Effort / Cost** | **High Effort / Cost** |
|---|---|---|
| **High Impact / Value** | **Quick Wins** *(Do these first)* | **Major Projects** *(Plan and schedule)* |
| **Low Impact / Value** | **Fill-Ins** *(Delegate or batch)* | **Drop / Avoid** *(Reconsider or ignore)* |


---

### How to Build and Use a Matrix

1. **List the work:** Gather all tasks, projects, or feature ideas into a single backlog.[[1]](https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence/templates/prioritization-matrix-whiteboard)[[2]](https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence/templates/prioritization-matrix)
2. **Define criteria:** Decide what matters most for your team (e.g., customer value, deadline, technical difficulty, or ROI).[[1]](https://www.smartsheet.com/priority-matrix-templates)[[2]](https://www.projectmanager.com/blog/prioritization-templates)
3. **Score or plot:** Rate each item or place it into the appropriate grid quadrant.[[1]](https://www.stratechi.com/prioritization-matrix/)
4. **Take action:** Focus your immediate resources on top-ranked items and push low-value, high-effort tasks to the bottom.[[1]](https://www.mural.co/templates/prioritization-matrix)[[2]](https://www.smartsheet.com/priority-matrix-templates)


---

### Free Digital Templates
You can find pre-built, ready-to-use templates on popular collaboration and spreadsheet platforms:

- **Whiteboard & Visual Grids:** [Miro Priority Matrix](https://miro.com/templates/priority-matrix/) or [Mural Prioritization Matrix](https://www.mural.co/templates/prioritization-matrix) [[1]](https://miro.com/templates/priority-matrix/)[[2]](https://www.mural.co/templates/prioritization-matrix)
- **Task & Project Trackers:** [Asana Prioritization Matrix Template](https://asana.com/templates/prioritization-matrix) or [Smartsheet Priority Matrix Templates](https://www.smartsheet.com/priority-matrix-templates) [[1]](https://www.smartsheet.com/priority-matrix-templates)[[2]](https://asana.com/templates/prioritization-matrix)

If you share **what kind of project or list you are working on** (daily tasks, product features, or team goals), I can help you pick the best framework and set up your scoring criteria.
